text: THE READING ROOM公開コード・データ / Public code and data Arbitrary Lagrangian–Eulerian methods Eulerian cells stay fixed while fluid crosses their faces. Lagrangian cells move with the fluid. In ALE, the mesh velocity w can be chosen independently of the fluid velocity u. Hirt, Amsden, and Cook (1974) provide a classical all-speed ALE formulation. The flux is relative to the moving face# Reynolds transport gives, for a moving control volume K(t), ddt∫K(t)U dV+∫∂K(t)[F(U)⋅n−(w⋅n)U]dS=0.dtd​∫K(t)​UdV+∫∂K(t)​[F(U)⋅n−(w⋅n)U]dS=0. With w = 0 this is Eulerian. Choosing the normal mesh speed equal to the fluid normal speed gives the Lagrangian mass-flux limit. Pressure still transfers momentum and energy across a material face; setting mass flux to zero does not set every Euler flux to zero. Geometry must obey a conservation law too# For a uniform state to remain uniform, changing cell volumes and face motion must agree: d∣K∣dt=∫∂Kw⋅n dS.dtd∣K∣​=∫∂K​w⋅ndS. Its discrete counterpart is the geometric conservation law (GCL). A mesh-motion routine and a flow update that use inconsistent swept volumes can create a spurious flow from constant data, even if each looks accurate separately. A reproducible one-step check# numart.geometry.moving_volume_uniform_test deforms faces on [0,1] by a smooth sinusoidal displacement with fixed endpoints. Face velocity is the actual displacement divided by delta t. For constant scalar q, it updates the extensive quantity Vq with relative flux (a−w)q and divides by the new volume. The same displacement appears in both operations. import numpy as np from numart.geometry import moving_volume_uniform_test old_faces, new_faces, q = moving_volume_uniform_test(phase=0.8) print(np.max(np.abs(q - 1))) Uniform-state preservation is checked to roundoff over several deformation phases. The amplitude restriction ensures positive cell widths. This is a 1D moving-volume identity check, not an ALE Euler solver or a test of accuracy for nonuniform data. Mesh motion, remapping, and distortion# A complete ALE method may move vertices, solve a Lagrangian or relative-flux step, and remap to a better mesh. Conservative remapping, mesh tangling, boundary motion, and temporal consistency require additional tests. A remap that preserves total mass can still violate positivity or fail to preserve a constant state. Use the mesh chapter to separate topology from motion, and the coordinate chapter to distinguish moving control volumes from changing tensor bases.
